spillover_issues.title: [levanter] Make the forced final checkpoint save crash-safe on temporary and restarted runs

spillover_issues.author: asonnino
spillover_issues.body:
**Summary.** After the last training step, `Trainer.train()` calls the checkpoint hook with `force=True`, and `Checkpointer.on_step(force=True)` saves that step again even when it was already saved, into the same `step-N/` directory, while the `metadata.json` from the first save (the commit marker) stays in place. On a local file system, a crash after the re-save has opened `manifest.json` for writing can leave `step-N/` looking committed but with an empty manifest, so every restart picks it and fails until an operator deletes it. We did not test object stores, where an object is replaced only when its write completes. The smallest fix we see is to write `manifest.json` through `atomic_rename`, as `_save_metadata` already does for `metadata.json` (see "Suggested fix"); we can open a PR for it. ## Affected versions - Reproduced on 2026-11-13 with the standalone script below on marin-levanter 0.2.274.dev43433851997 and 0.2.268.dev43309064464, and on marin `main` at [`a922ffc`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/a922ffc740488a3aa82c8ac3f8cf8e9dd8d77ba7) (its `levanter` package installed over the 0.2.274 wheel, which it matches file for file), TensorStore 0.1.84, JAX 0.12.0.1 on CPU, local file system. It also reproduced on 2026-11-10 on 0.2.260.dev42827925033 and on `main` at `2b3b0a04`. - The links below pin `4aab2cff`. At `a922ffc`, `checkpoint.py`, `tensorstore_serialization.py` and `checkpoint_manifest.py` are unchanged, and the linked lines of `trainer.py` are two lines further down with the same content. ## Impact - **Loud**: every restart fails with `ValidationError: 1 validation error for CheckpointManifest ... Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0 [type=json_invalid, input_value='', input_type=str]`. - **Needs an operator** to delete `step-N/` (or its `metadata.json`). If `step-N` was the run's first permanent checkpoint (the `--permanent` case below), no loadable checkpoint is left and the run then restarts from scratch; otherwise the previous permanent checkpoint remains. - **No operator action** is needed to trigger it, whenever the last step was already saved before the forced save: - the last step is a multiple of a `keep` `every` interval (a permanent save). The forced save is permanent too and goes to the same `step-N/` under `base_path`, so this holds whether or not `temporary_base_path` is set; - the `save_interval` timer fires on the last step (a temporary save), with `temporary_base_path` unset (the default); - from the code (not tested): a completed run is restarted, since `train()` then runs the forced hooks for the step it loaded ([trainer.py#L618-L625](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L618-L625)). [#9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) reports this re-save on a resume from the final step, where it fails for another reason. - The window is short: from opening `manifest.json`, one small JSON file, to the end of its write. We injected crashes only into this file of the re-save; the array data of the re-save goes into the same OCDBT database and was not tested. ## Reproduction Standalone script (single process, JAX on CPU), in the collapsible block below. It drives `Checkpointer` the way `Trainer.train()` does and kills the process right after the forced re-save opens `step-N/manifest.json` for writing.
levanter_final_resave.py ```python """Levanter: a crash during the end-of-training re-save of an already-saved step leaves it unloadable. python levanter_final_resave.py [--permanent] Run 1 saves steps 1 to 3 (step 2 permanent because every=2, steps 1 and 3 temporary because save_interval has elapsed), then makes the forced save that Trainer.train() makes after its last step (Checkpointer.on_step(force=True)) into the same step-3/ directory, and is killed right after that save opens step-3/manifest.json for writing. With --permanent, run 1 stops at step 2, so the forced save rewrites the permanent step-2/. Run 2 discovers the latest checkpoint and loads it. """ import builtins import datetime import os import subprocess import sys import tempfile import time import jax.numpy as jnp from levanter.checkpoint import Checkpointer, CheckpointInterval, latest_checkpoint_path, load_checkpoint STATE = {"model": jnp.arange(4.0)} LAST = 2 if "--permanent" in sys.argv else 3 def checkpointer(base): return Checkpointer(base, save_interval=datetime.timedelta(milliseconds=1), step_policies=[CheckpointInterval(every=2)]) if __name__ == "__main__": if sys.argv[1:2] == ["crash"]: ckpt = checkpointer(sys.argv[2]) for step in range(1, LAST + 1): time.sleep(0.01) ckpt.on_step(tree=STATE, step=step) ckpt.wait_until_finished() real_open = builtins.open def crashing_open(file, mode="r", *args, **kwargs): f = real_open(file, mode, *args, **kwargs) if str(file).endswith(f"step-{LAST}/manifest.json") and "w" in mode: os._exit(137) # the file has just been opened for writing, so it is now empty return f builtins.open = crashing_open ckpt.on_step(tree=STATE, step=LAST, force=True) # what Trainer.train() does after the last step sys.exit("not killed") base = tempfile.mkdtemp() rc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, __file__, "crash", base] + sys.argv[1:]).returncode print(f"run 1 killed (exit {rc}); checkpoints: {sorted(os.listdir(base))}; step-{LAST}/: " f"{sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(base, f'step-{LAST}')))}", flush=True) path = latest_checkpoint_path(base) print(f"latest checkpoint: {os.path.basename(path)}", flush=True) try: load_checkpoint(STATE, path) print("loaded") except Exception as e: print(f"load failed: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:300]}") ```
Output on 0.2.274.dev43433851997 (the same on 0.2.268.dev43309064464 and on marin `main` at `a922ffc`; pydantic's help link removed): ```text $ python levanter_final_resave.py run 1 killed (exit 137); checkpoints: ['step-2', 'step-3']; step-3/: ['d', 'manifest.json', 'manifest.ocdbt', 'metadata.json'] latest checkpoint: step-3 load failed: ValidationError: 1 validation error for CheckpointManifest Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0 [type=json_invalid, input_value='', input_type=str] $ python levanter_final_resave.py --permanent run 1 killed (exit 137); checkpoints: ['step-2']; step-2/: ['d', 'manifest.json', 'manifest.ocdbt', 'metadata.json'] latest checkpoint: step-2 load failed: ValidationError: 1 validation error for CheckpointManifest Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0 [type=json_invalid, input_value='', input_type=str] ``` In the second case no loadable checkpoint is left. ## Expected vs actual - Expected: the final step that was already committed stays loadable; at most its `is_temporary` flag changes. - Actual: the committed `step-N/` is rewritten in place under its old `metadata.json`, and a crash during the rewrite makes it unloadable while discovery still selects it. ## Root cause 1. [`train()`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L627-L638) runs the hooks once more with `force=True` after the loop, for the same step whose regular hooks already ran inside [`train_step`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L571); the [checkpoint hook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/trainer.py#L656-L662) passes `force` to `Checkpointer.on_step`. 2. [`on_step`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L605-L607) skips an already saved step only when `force` is false, and the forced save always uses [`destination = f"step-{step}"`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L644-L670) under `base_path`, which is the directory of the first save when that save was permanent or `temporary_base_path` is unset. `save_checkpoint` reuses it ([`fs.makedirs(plain_path, exist_ok=True)`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L866)). 3. Process 0 then rewrites `manifest.json` in place ([tensorstore_serialization.py#L645-L648](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/tensorstore_serialization.py#L645-L648), [`write_manifest`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint_manifest.py#L64-L65), a plain `StoragePath.write_text`, which on a local path truncates the file when it opens it), while the old `metadata.json` remains. Discovery treats any directory with a `metadata.json` as complete ([checkpoint.py#L1245-L1246](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L1245-L1246)), so it selects the half-rewritten step. [`_save_metadata`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L931-L947), by contrast, writes `metadata.json` through `atomic_rename` on local paths. [`Checkpointer.save_final_checkpoint`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/4aab2cff9e0a7d105928ba0bdc575ee5c43c6610/lib/levanter/src/levanter/checkpoint.py#L752-L757) already skips a step whose last save was permanent, but `Trainer.train()` does not call it (its callers are `tests/test_checkpoint.py` and five grug training scripts), and it still re-saves a temporary step into the same directory. ## Suggested fix From the smallest: 1. Write `manifest.json` through `atomic_rename` on local paths, as `_save_metadata` does for `metadata.json`. With this change as a monkeypatch on 0.2.268, and the kill moved to the opening of the temporary file, both modes of the script load the checkpoint after the crash, and a `manifest.json.tmp.` file is left next to `manifest.json`. It does not change when a re-save happens. The array data of the re-save, which goes into the same OCDBT database, was not tested. 2. Or, on local paths, uncommit first (remote permanent prefixes can deny deletes, as PR [#9215](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9215) describes): remove `metadata.json` before saving into a committed directory and write it back once the manifest and data are complete, so that a crash leaves the step ignored by discovery instead of selected and unloadable. If `step-N/` was the run's first permanent checkpoint, the next run would then start from scratch without an error (not tested; unlike item 1, this gives up the old checkpoint). 3. Or do not re-serialize a step that is already committed: skip the forced save when the last save of that step was permanent, as `save_final_checkpoint` does; when it was temporary and in the same directory, wait for that save to finish, then rewrite only `metadata.json` with `is_temporary: false` (through `_save_metadata`), drop the path from `self._temporary_checkpoints` and prune as the permanent-save callback does. PR [#9416](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9416) proposed a skip for the no-op resume and was closed, so 1 or 2 may fit better. ## Prior reports and related issues We found no prior report of this crash consequence. The re-save itself has been reported failing for another reason: - [#9380](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9380) (open): "[levanter] Final checkpoint rewrite fails on resume with changed chunk shape". Resuming a run from its final step makes Levanter force another write into the existing `step-N` path, which fails when the resumed run writes a different chunk shape; [#6253](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6253) (closed) had the same failure. PR [#9416](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9416) ("[levanter] Skip checkpoint rewrite on no-op resume") was closed unmerged on 2026-09-25 with the comment "this isn't the right fix, the upstream issue is related to a sharding mismatch", and the open PR [#10786](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10786) proposes a fix for that mismatch. The crash window here does not depend on a layout change: the script above rewrites the same layout. - [#10453](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10453) (open): resuming into a root with uncommitted partial checkpoints fails the next save. A different trigger, but it also comes from saving into a fixed `step-N/` destination; it proposes a fresh directory per save. - [#5386](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5386) (open): retention after a corrupted multihost resume ([#5319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5319)) left one trustworthy permanent checkpoint. A different cause, but it shows the cost when the newest checkpoint cannot be used. - [#2831](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2831) (closed): fault-tolerance validation, which listed "verify async checkpoints are atomic" as a goal. - PR [#9215](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9215): how `metadata.json` is committed on remote storage. - PR [#10969](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10969) (open): lock files for multi-process OCDBT commits on NFS; it also removes `*.__lock` files that a killed process left in a reused `step-N/`. It changes `tensorstore_serialization.py` too, but concerns the OCDBT `manifest.ocdbt`, not `manifest.json`.
Searches (run on 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-12) GitHub issue and pull request search, which `gh search issues` also uses: `repo:marin-community/marin` with `checkpoint manifest.json` (27 results), `temporary checkpoint final save` (79), `checkpoint atomic` (73), `checkpoint corrupt resume` (27), `checkpoint DATA_LOSS` (0), `tensorstore_checkpoint` (0); `repo:marin-community/levanter` with `checkpoint manifest`, `checkpoint corrupt`, `checkpoint atomic`, `checkpoint crash resume`, `temporary checkpoint final` (nothing relevant). Results were read by title, and the candidates above were read in full. Web search: `Levanter checkpoint manifest.json empty CheckpointManifest json_invalid after crash final checkpoint save` (found #2831 and downstream projects' notes on draining asynchronous commits at exit, none about this). On 2026-11-12, threads created since 2026-11-10 (read by title) and issues updated since then with `"final checkpoint"`, `"temporary checkpoint"`, `save_final_checkpoint`, `CheckpointManifest` or `manifest.json`: nothing related.
## How this was found We found this with a crash-injection tool that kills every process with SIGKILL just before or just after each file operation of a checkpoint save, restarts the job with the same configuration and checks what it resumed. The standalone script above reproduces it without that tool. ### AI assistance This report, its reproduction script and the analysis were prepared with an AI coding agent. I ran the reproduction on the versions listed above and checked the analysis and the cited code. If you track such reports with the `agent-generated` label, please add it; I seem unable to set labels.

comments.author: asonnino
comments.body:
I re-ran the script from this issue against #11552 (merged as bc25c57). It fixes the `--permanent` case. The default case, where the last step was a temporary save, still leaves `step-3/` unloadable.

Versions, all on 2026-11-21 with TensorStore 0.1.84 and JAX 0.12.1 on CPU, local file system:

- marin-levanter 0.2.328.dev44898056838, built from `main` at `b0536cf`, which includes bc25c57;
- `main` at [`cb991a5`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/cb991a5a5c8af4d670d56757eeae3e59edd4a778), its `levanter` package installed over that wheel;
- marin-levanter 0.2.274.dev43433851997, the release in the report, as a control.

Output on 0.2.328 and on `main` (the same on both; pydantic's help link removed):

```text
$ python levanter_final_resave.py
run 1 killed (exit 137); checkpoints: ['step-2', 'step-3']; step-3/: ['d', 'manifest.json', 'manifest.ocdbt', 'metadata.json']
latest checkpoint: step-3
load failed: ValidationError: 1 validation error for CheckpointManifest
  Invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0 [type=json_invalid, input_value='', input_type=str]

$ python levanter_final_resave.py --permanent
not killed
run 1 killed (exit 1); checkpoints: ['step-2']; step-2/: ['d', 'manifest.json', 'manifest.ocdbt', 'metadata.json']
latest checkpoint: step-2
loaded
```

With `--permanent`, the forced save now returns at the new check in `on_step` without writing, so the script's kill when `step-2/manifest.json` is opened never fires: run 1 ends with the script's `not killed` (exit status 1), and `step-2` loads. On 0.2.274 both modes still fail as in the report.

What remains:

- The last step was a temporary save (the `save_interval` timer fired on it) and `temporary_base_path` is unset, which is the script's default mode. `_last_save_permanent` is false, so the forced save still rewrites `step-N/` in place under its old `metadata.json`, and a crash while `manifest.json` is open leaves the step selected by discovery and unloadable. The PR description says the same ("Temporary final saves ... still rewrite the step path").
- From the code, not tested: restarting a completed run creates a new `Checkpointer` with `_last_save_step = 0`, so the forced hooks in `train()` rewrite the loaded step even when it was saved as permanent. The PR description notes this too.

`write_manifest` still writes `manifest.json` in place, so item 1 of the suggested fix (writing it through `atomic_rename`) still applies to both cases, and item 3 to the temporary one. I can open a PR for either.

This comment and the analysis were prepared with an AI coding agent. I ran the reproduction on the versions listed above and checked the analysis and the cited code.

spillover_issues.title: [levanter] A crash during the forced final re-save of a committed `step-N/` can leave it unloadable

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

A 6-hour optimization sprint (started 2026-11-21 ~13:45 UTC / 8:45 AM EST) measured Mochi (535B-A23B) decode and rollout throughput on GB200s and **selected the training geometry: EP16/DP16/TP1, seq64, HBM 0.85, batch 8192 (A10, 48 trainer + 16 rollout = 64 GB200)** — 2.169x the `.103` control's per-GPU rollout rate. Best pure-decode serving result: EP16/seqs64/HBM90 at 831.73 tok/s/GPU (a fixed-prompt-pool upper bound, not a training gain). The real Mochi RL training launch is planned for 2026-11-21 ~19:45 UTC (14:45 EST) on cw-us-east-08a. This issue is maintained by the secretary agent from the worker's REPORT.md/STATUS.md; every measured arm is recorded below with reproduction details.

## Description

Context: the long-loop plan needs ~50B SFT tokens in a 20 h stage plus RL rounds on Mochi. Today Mochi decodes ~10 tok/s per request and ~25 tok/s per GB200 at eval concurrency, and Mochi SFT trains ~143–177k tok/s per rack (#8089: 29.3 s/step on 11 racks). The sprint replaces back-of-envelope ceilings (decode ~2–4k tok/s/GPU BF16 at large batch; training ~2–3x the current rate) with measurements.

Two lanes:

- **A — real-RL rollout arms**: full round-runner RL jobs (48 trainer + 12 rollout GB200, two optimizer updates), measuring rollout throughput under admission knobs; each arm is cancelled after its measured 25-min window.
- **B — pure-decode capacity arms**: no trainer; the checked-in long-loop throughput worker serves a 6.4k-prompt / 1k-output synthetic workload (plus replay variants) and measures sustained decode; arms run to a valid counter window then are cancelled.

Fixed infrastructure for all arms: cluster `cw-us-east-08a`, PRODUCTION priority, GB200 GPUs, rack r136 hard-excluded, one-NVLink-gang placement, BF16, FLASH_ATTN + triton MoE, prefix caching, compilation + PIECEWISE CUDA graphs on.

Workload-shape caveat for the B serving lane: the fixed-pool shared8 arms use 32 prompt bodies / 256 request identities at 6,439 input / 1,024 output tokens (long) or 139 input (short); repeated cycles can overstate fresh-RL prefix reuse. Pure serving runs use 12 GPUs unless the arm name says EP16 (then 16). All B arms use 0 Daytona vCPU.

### Reproduction

- Repo: `marin-community/marin`, branch `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` and sprint branch `benfeuer/mochi-throughput`.
- Round configs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-throughput-*.yaml` (default-2update, inflight128, staleness11, engine32-kv85, harbor1024, harbor384, ep16-seqs64, ep16-seqs64-kv90, ep16-httpid-control, noquotas, kv-fp8, **ep16-demand512** `.118`, **train** `.115`; the retired workers128 config was deleted unlaunched).
- Decode specs: `experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/mochi-decode-*.json` (seqs16 control through the ep16 variants).
- Launch commands:

### Rollout concurrency (code trace)

- `TaskRolloutWorker` holds `task_slots` and `harbor_task_slots` semaphores (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_worker.py:390-391`), acquired per task (`:548-552`); the Harbor semaphore wraps the entire `engine.run_task`.
- Harbor `n_concurrent_trials` is consumed at `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/inline_harbor_client.py:119`.
- Documented rule: slots = Harbor `n_concurrent_trials` (16 when unset) // num workers (`lib/skyrlrecipe/src/skyrlrecipe/sections.py:458`); config key `terminal_bench.harbor.n_concurrent_trials` (`experiments/post_training/long_loop/stage_config.py:38`). For the 256-slot config that is 8/worker; Harbor384 gives 12/worker.
- Precision: the 8-slot semaphore is one group's worth, not an atomic group lock — partial groups can interleave; dispatch `min(_pending)` has no Harbor-slot awareness, and the generic 1024/worker task slots are unbinding.
- Measurement limit: no explicit Harbor-semaphore wait logs are emitted, and A5's bounded logs contain 0 direct slot-wait records, so actual Harbor occupancy is NOT measured; A3's 128 group calls / 430 pending model requests do not count Harbor occupancy.
- Staleness admission: `FullBatch.lease_batch` uses `range(step, step + staleness + 1)`, so staleness can change admission during step 1 even without a policy update (this corrects an earlier blanket "never binds" statement; the A2 causal-gain claim remains withdrawn and default staleness 3 is kept per direction).
- Consumed route quotas require `batch_policy: full_batch` (`vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/buffer.py:49,72`; `lib/skyrlrecipe/src/skyrlrecipe/sections.py:440,444`).

A 6-hour optimization sprint (started 2026-11-21 ~13:45 UTC / 8:45 AM EST) is measuring Mochi (535B-A23B) decode and rollout throughput on GB200s to pick the config for the first real long-loop RL training run. ## Description

Context: the long-loop plan needs ~50B SFT tokens in a 20 h stage plus RL rounds on Mochi. - **B — pure-decode capacity arms**: no trainer; the checked-in long-loop throughput worker serves a 6.4k-prompt / 1k-output synthetic workload (plus replay variants) and measures sustained decode; arms run to a valid counter window then are cancelled.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

#11954 is an active configuration sweep, with the config changes already on [#11120](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11120), rather than a standalone code fix. A3 measured 127.22 tok/s/GPU over its first 25 minutes versus 55.90 for the control, but both rates are console-sample estimates without native generation-token counters. Harbor384 `.109` was submitted at `c6515fbdc7bc2b51f0f43649dac08ee54fa3397d` with native `inference_stats` counters and a worst-case 1536 vCPU sandbox load. The 1321.42 tok/s/GPU seqs128 result uses a short synthetic prompt workload, so it cannot establish the real-rollout winner.

**Relevant code**
- [Harbor384 round config](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6515fbdc7bc2b51f0f43649dac08ee54fa3397d/experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-throughput-harbor384.yaml) — candidate with native counters
- [A3 round config](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/c6515fbdc7bc2b51f0f43649dac08ee54fa3397d/experiments/post_training/long_loop/rounds/mochi-throughput-engine32-kv85.yaml) — current rollout baseline

# Proposed Fix

1. Measure Harbor384 over an aligned first-25-minute window. Record reset-safe native generated-token deltas, rollout GPU count, running requests, KV usage, sandbox count, and quota events; label the A3 comparison as approximate because its counter source differs.
2. Finish the two pending EP16 decode arms. Treat their synthetic rates as candidates for a real-rollout validation arm, with the same prompt mix and measurement window, before changing the training config.
3. Test the planned 128-worker, 1-CPU-per-worker client arm with the other A3 settings held fixed. Keep the Daytona sandbox load within the shared quota and the A-arm footprint within two racks.
4. At the 19:30 UTC decision point, select the highest sustainable real-rollout rate that meets the resource limits; keep A3 as the provisional fallback if no later arm improves on it. Pin the selected config and source SHA in #11120, record the counter window and run receipt here, then use that pinned config for the planned 19:45 UTC launch.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
Parent: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11535

## Summary

- **Motivation:** 64-H100 Snowball SFT runs on `cw-us-east-02a` train at two distinct speeds (~44–55 s vs. ~120–128 s per update); in the slow mode, a 150-update job needs ~5.0–5.3 h and cannot fit a 4 h wall-time limit. Across 33 audited runs, the slow mode coincides with compiling `jit_train_step` in-job rather than loading a cached executable, and using a compile pre-job avoids it in practice.
- **Goal:** Determine whether in-job compilation vs. persistent compilation-cache hit causes the two-speed split on 64 H100, and test the candidate per-rank autotune-fetch divergence mechanism.
- **Data:** Read-only audit of 33 existing 64-H100 Snowball SFT runs (W&B, Finelog, S3 compilation-cache and autotune-store listings, and source), plus two queued controlled runs on the same configuration.
- **Method:** Correlational audit across 33 runs (including three natural pairs), source audit of Iris `compile_cache.py` and JAX v0.11.1 persistent caching, followed by two queued tests: (1) a cache-hit control (restarting an in-job-compiled arm unchanged in the same region to load its own cached executable) and (2) a per-rank executable-fingerprint test after an in-job compile.
- **Results:** Observational audit complete (correlational; causal tests queued). On `cw-us-east-02a`, 6 of 6 slow runs (124.8–128.1 s/update; plus 3 compile pre-jobs at 120–122 s/update and `control-prelude-20261118` at 121–122 s/update) compiled `jit_train_step` in-job and showed asymmetric GPU power (GPU0 185–221 W vs. GPU1 444–489 W), whereas 0 of 20 phase-logged fast runs (44.1–54.5 s/update) wrote a new entry and all showed symmetric power (221–337 W). On `cw-rno2a`, two runs loading an executable compiled against a cold autotune store ran at an intermediate third speed (81.0 and 89.9 s/update) with symmetric power (411–434 W).
- **Conclusion:** In-job compile vs. cache hit is a clean correlational discriminator, while the candidate mechanism remains unproven (specifically whether XLA at `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0` changes kernel selection across fetched vs. unfetched per-fusion autotune directories). Practically, a compile pre-job avoids the slow mode because the main run loads process 0's cached executable.

## Observational findings (correlational)

- **Slow mode on `cw-us-east-02a` (6 of 6 slow runs at `124.8–128.1 s/update`):** Every slow run wrote a new `jit_train_step-*` entry to `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/compilation-cache` during its own first-step compile window. First-step compile took `24.6–32.6 s` across the 5 Finelog-logged slow runs; in the 6th (`c150-base-lr5e5-noclip-1118eager-20261120`, 128.1 s/update), the task-0 journal recorded `19.1 s` on rank 0 vs. `31.9–33.6 s` on ranks 1–7 (rank 0 ended at `22:54:46.6Z`, matching cache write `04f6f474`). Three additional compile pre-jobs measured `120–122 s/update` with the same power split (`GPU0` `213–227 W` vs. `GPU1` `460–511 W`).
- **Fast mode on `cw-us-east-02a` (0 of 20 phase-logged fast runs at `44.1–54.5 s/update`):** None wrote a new `jit_train_step-*` entry in its compile window; first-step compile took `9.0–18.5 s`. Six fast `6164muonh` / 11-19 runs used 5 per-arm cache directories whose single entry (`61378ece`) had been written beforehand by a compile pre-job.
- **Mode stays fixed for the entire run:** Over 360 updates (`eighthour-fp32-warm-a`), 60-update block medians remained `124.7–128.2 s` (p10–p90 `119.7–133.5 s`, range `114.7–240.8 s`); no audited run switched modes.
- **GPU power signature (W&B, rank-0 node):** Slow runs draw `185–221 W` on GPU0 vs. `444–489 W` on GPU1; fast runs draw `221–337 W` symmetrically across GPU0 and GPU1. A single-snapshot capture across all 8 nodes of `c150-base-lr5e5-noclip-1118eager-20261120` showed local GPU0 at `220–239 W` (`0–24%` memory utilization) vs. GPUs 1–7 at `468–542 W` on 7 of 8 nodes, and all 8 GPUs at `191–234 W` on the 8th node.
- **Three natural pairs (same tree and optimizer):**

| Slow run (compiled in-job) | s/update | Fast twin (loaded; no new write) | s/update | Config difference |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| `eighthour-fp32-repeat` | 127.4 | `eighthour-fp32-control` (started 48 min later) | 46.9 | `data.control_only`, `data.repair_once` |
| `eighthour-fp32-warm-a` | 126.3 | `eighthour-fp32-warm-a-control-r2` | 46.4 | `data.control_only`, `data.repair_once` |
| `c150-base-control-prelude-20261118` (wrote key `22ca1369`) | 121–122 | `c150-base-control-eager-20261118` | 45.5 | Cache hit vs. miss on same key `22ca1369` |

  *(Caveat: without JAX cache-miss debug logs on those runs, loading the slow twin's specific entry is inferred from the cache listing and absence of a new write.)*
- **Third mode on `cw-rno2a` (`81.0` and `89.9 s/update`, symmetric power):** `replay10-1118eager-rno2a` (`81.0 s`, GPU0 `415.6 W` / GPU1 `429.5 W`) and `replay40-1118eager-rno2a-r2` (`89.9 s`, GPU0 `411.5 W` / GPU1 `434.2 W`) both loaded `jit_train_step-22ca1369` written at `20:58:40.81Z` by the initial `replay40-rno2a` attempt. That initial attempt started at `20:52:12Z`, before `xla-per-fusion-autotune/21d037aa47` was created on `cw-rno2a` (`20:52:45Z`), so no rank fetched a tuned autotune set (though local `/cache` state on those nodes was not listed). Whether a tuned executable on `cw-rno2a` matches `02a`'s ~45–50 s is unproven because the regions also differ in hardware and fabric.
- **Practical impact:** Slow runs (~120–128 s/update) cannot complete 150 updates inside a 4 h job limit (~5.0–5.3 h). Using a compile pre-job avoids the slow mode in practice; `compile_cache_worker.py` also enforces a persistent-cache hit on main runs that follow a pre-job.

## Factors ruled out

| Factor | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Bad node or rack | Ruled out as main cause | No node appears in all 6 slow runs (max 3/6); the 4 most-shared nodes each appear in 5–8 fast runs. `c150-base-lr5e5-noclip-1118eager-20261120` (128.1 s) ran on the exact 8 nodes where `replay40-6164muonh-8h-u500` ran at 50.4 s (finished ~1 h earlier). |
| Region congestion / concurrent jobs | Ruled out | Slow `repeat` and `warm-a` overlapped in time with fast `eighthour-control` and `single` on `cw-us-east-02a`. |
| GPU memory | Ruled out | Identical per-GPU allocation (`76.0 GiB` GPU0, `63.1–63.2 GiB` GPUs 1–7) in 32 of 33 runs (only a rematerialized fast run differed: `66.2 / 62.4–62.5 GiB`). |
| Clocks / thermals | Ruled out (1 snapshot) | SM clocks `1815–1830 MHz` across all GPUs, `31–59 °C` (GPU0 SW power-cap throttle bit `0x4` also appears at `225 W` under load). |
| Data loading / checkpoints / hooks | Ruled out | Slow arm task-0 journal: `data_loading` median `0.0 s` vs. `train_step` median `125.7 s` over 48 spans. |
| Tree hash, BF16/FP32, carried restore | Ruled out as discriminators | Each value appears in both fast and slow runs. |
| CuTeDSL kernel cache | Ruled out | All 8 ranks logged `5` hits and `0` misses in both a fast and a slow run. |
| Runtime flags / env | Ruled out | `worker_runtime_settings` lines are identical (`--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`, eager, identical `XLA_FLAGS`). |
| InfiniBand error counters | Not attributable | 7 of 8 slow-arm nodes had non-zero cumulative `local_ack_timeout_err` / `req_cqe_error` (the 8th had `0` on both, `1` `port_rcv_errors`, `1` `excessive_buffer_overrun_errors`), with no pre-run baseline and prior fast runs on the same nodes. |

## Candidate mechanism (source-verified path; XLA level-0 link unproven)

`lib/iris/src/iris/jax/compile_cache.py` is byte-identical (`sha256 a811075a`) at commits `6164fcbd`, `daa85ddf`, `3b291b10`, and `main` `eecb397a0c`; all three experiment trees run JAX v0.11.1:

- **One fetcher per node (`compile_cache.py:148-166`, `lib/iris/src/iris/jax/init.py:191`):** `_autotune_cache_role()` assigns global process `0` as `UPLOADER`, the first local rank on every other node (`process_index % processes_per_task == 0`, `:164`) as `FETCHER`, and the remaining 7 local ranks per node as `NONE` (`:166`).
- **Per-process autotune directories (`compile_cache.py:95-98, 112-116`, `lib/finestore/src/finestore/fileset.py:76`):** Each process gets `/cache/xla/per-fusion-autotune/process-<global index>`. `UPLOADER` syncs (fetching at init) and `FETCHER` fetches into its own directory; `NONE` ranks do not fetch (their node-local `/cache` folders are **not fetched**, though not guaranteed empty because `/cache` persists across jobs on a node).
- **Persistent cache key ignores the autotune directory (JAX v0.11.1):** `jax/_src/cache_key.py:300` lists `--xla_gpu_per_fusion_autotune_cache_dir` among flags excluded from the cache key, `:391` skips it when hashing `XLA_FLAGS`, and `:349` blanks it in hashed compile options. `compile_cache.py:61` sets `jax_persistent_cache_enable_xla_caches="none"`, leaving JAX's own autotune-cache mode logic (`jax/_src/compiler.py:318-324`) inactive.
- **Process 0 writes the shared executable (JAX v0.11.1 `jax/_src/compiler.py:835`):** Only `process_id == 0` writes a persistent cache entry. On a subsequent cache hit, all 64 ranks deserialize process 0's executable (compiled by the `UPLOADER`).
- **Unproven link:** Whether `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0` with unfetched sibling folders actually produces different (default) kernels vs. fetched tuned folders lives in XLA C++ (`jaxlib` 0.11.1) and is **not verified from source**. If XLA skips the per-fusion cache lookup at level 0, this candidate mechanism fails.

## Planned tests (queued)

1. **Cache-hit control:** Restart an in-job-compiled arm unchanged in the same region so it hits its own cached executable instead of compiling in-job (pre-registered prediction if the in-job-compile hypothesis holds: ~45–55 s/update, ~9–19 s compile, no new write, symmetric GPU power; ~125 s/update if refuted).
2. **Per-rank executable fingerprint test (decisive for the candidate mechanism):** Log `(rank, _fingerprint, _executable_text_sha256)` on all ranks after an in-job compile (`compile_cache_worker.py` currently records rank 0 only). If ranks 1–7 differ from rank 0 (and rank 8 matches rank 0), per-rank executable divergence is confirmed; if all 8 match, the candidate mechanism is refuted.

## Possibly related

- https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11793: All 8 first-update hangs documented in issue 11793 (7 concurrent cold + 1 solo cold) were also in-job compiles. No causal link between the two-speed mode and the hangs is claimed here.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 This extends https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11775, which first reported the effect with a controlled test (miss/hit on one cache key `jit_train_step-61378ece…`, the short warm-up workaround, and matching rank-0 executable fingerprint and compiled-text SHA-256 between miss and hit).

## What this issue adds

- A 33-run audit across 64-H100 Snowball SFT runs (6/6 slow runs compiled in-job; 0/20 phase-logged fast runs wrote a new entry).
- The per-GPU power asymmetry on slow runs: local GPU0 at ~185–239 W vs. ~444–542 W on the remaining GPUs per node (against symmetric 221–337 W on fast runs).
- A third intermediate speed on `cw-rno2a` (81.0 and 89.9 s/update with symmetric power) after compiling against a cold autotune store.
- Source verification of Iris's one-fetcher-per-node autotune role (`lib/iris/src/iris/jax/compile_cache.py:148-166`) and JAX v0.11.1 persistent caching.
- A queued per-rank executable-fingerprint test after an in-job compile.

## How the two findings fit

- Issue 11775 found process 0's executable fingerprint and compiled-text SHA-256 identical between miss and hit. Because only process 0 writes the persistent cache entry (JAX v0.11.1 `jax/_src/compiler.py:835`) and process 0 is also the `UPLOADER` that fetches the autotune set, identical process-0 executables across miss and hit match a per-rank difference on ranks 1–7, but do not prove it.
- Issue 11775 listed the per-fusion autotune cache as ruled out by comparing two trees' stored sets (131,051 of 131,072 sampled keys matched). That comparison checks the remote stored sets across trees and does not cover per-rank `/cache/xla/per-fusion-autotune/process-<global index>` folder contents on a node during an in-job compile.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The 33-run audit in this issue links the slow mode to an in-job `jit_train_step` compile, but does not establish the cause. The controlled miss/hit pair in [#11775](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11775) changed from about 122 to 42–49 s/update with the same cache key and matching rank-0 executable hashes. Iris fetches the per-fusion autotune set on one process per node; the other seven processes use separate local directories, so per-rank executable divergence remains a testable hypothesis.

**Relevant code**
- [`compile_cache.py#L95-L116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/eecb397a0c29ef3cf0c123028a53df304a249b77/lib/iris/src/iris/jax/compile_cache.py#L95-L116) — per-process autotune directories and fetch.
- [`compile_cache.py#L148-L166`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/eecb397a0c29ef3cf0c123028a53df304a249b77/lib/iris/src/iris/jax/compile_cache.py#L148-L166) — uploader, fetcher, and unfetched roles.
- [`train.py#L1743-L1771`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/454902f11d08aaaf89bb8b177896a533aabb6db5/experiments/post_training/long_loop/sft_runtime/train.py#L1743-L1771) — first-step compile and dispatch.

# Proposed Fix

1. Complete the queued same-region restart of one slow arm with identical source, image, XLA flags, shapes, and cache URI. Verify a cache hit on all 64 ranks, then report steady-step medians, rank-local GPU power, and any new cache writes. A fast restart supports a cache-dependent mode; a slow restart rejects that prediction for this arm.
2. On a cold compile, record each rank's executable fingerprint and compiled-text SHA-256, plus the autotune directory's file count and digest before compilation. Compare rank 0, local ranks 1–7, and the first rank on the next node. These diagnostics should identify whether the unfetched ranks compile a different executable.
3. Capture short, matched steady-step XPlane traces from the cold job and its cache-hit restart. Compare kernel names, GEMM tile choices, per-kernel time, and idle gaps at the same update; verify that profiling preserves the speed ordering.
4. Change Iris cache materialization only if rank divergence and kernel evidence support it. Qualify that change with repeated cold/hit pairs on the same 8×8 H100 geometry, finite losses, no first-step stalls, and cold steady-step time within 10% of the hit run. If executable and kernel choices match, investigate post-compile runtime state instead.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **Two results: issue 11775 context, and the cw-rno2a A-r2 control.**

## Relation to issue 11775

Issue 11775 (https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11775) reported this effect first. The same `jit_train_step` runs about 122 s/step in the process that compiled it and about 45 s/step when loaded from the persistent cache. It includes a controlled miss/hit pair and the warm-up workaround. This audit confirms that report; it is not a new finding.

What this audit adds:
- **More runs:** 6 of 6 slow cw-us-east-02a runs compiled in-job, and 0 of 20 fast runs with a phase log did. There is also a same-key pair: control-prelude compiled `22ca1369` in-job and ran at 121-122 s; control-eager loaded it and ran at 45.5 s.
- **Per-rank signs:** in slow runs GPU0 draws 185-221 W against 444-489 W on GPU1. In arm A, rank 0 compiled in 19.1 s and ranks 1-7 in 31.9-33.6 s.
- **A code path:** `compile_cache.py` lets 1 rank per node fetch the tuned autotune set. A cache hit gives every rank process 0's executable.

How 11775's facts bear on the per-rank mechanism:
- **11775's matching fingerprints are rank 0's only.** Rank 0 is the rank that fetches the tuned set, so a match there fits the mechanism. It does not test ranks 1-7.
- **11775's profile was not on rank 0.** It was on **process 3**, on global rank 0's node (`local_device_ids=[3]`).
  - The readable trace has GPU events only for `/device:GPU:3`: 149,766 events, 450.8 s of device time, 299.7 s in GEMM fusions over steps 5-8.
  - Process 3 fetches no tuned set, so this fits "ranks 1-7 untuned". It is not proof: there is no slow-process trace of rank 0 and no fast-process trace of rank 3.
  - A slow-process trace of rank 0 showing the same small-tile GEMMs would refute the mechanism.
- **Trace files:** one other node file tested is corrupt. Per-rank profiles need per-process file names.

## cw-rno2a control: arm A relaunched (`c150-base-lr5e5-noclip-1118eager-20261120-rno2a-r2`)

These predictions were registered before the run reached step 0. The rno2a cache held no copy of arm A's program, and the rno2a autotune store was populated.

| feature | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|
| s/update | 120-128 s | 128.4, 121.5 and 123.6 s for updates 2-4 (update 1, which includes the compile: 172.8 s). The other rno2a arms run the same tree and 11-18 eager recipe at lr 2e-5 / clip 1.0 (key `22ca1369`) at 81-90 s. |
| power, rank-0 node (W&B medians after update 1) | GPU0 about 185-230 W, GPU1 about 440-510 W | GPU0 226 W; GPU1-7 476-526 W |
| new rno2a train-step entry while compiling | yes | `jit_train_step-04f6f474…` at 23:35:27Z: the same key as arm A's cw-us-east-02a executable |
| first-step compile | 25-33 s | not comparable: this code logs no phase lines. Rank 0 took about 21 s. |

**Reading:** 3 of the 4 features were met, and the 4th could not be measured. This fits the per-rank mechanism. It still needs the per-rank executable fingerprint test.

comments.body:
🤖 **Correction: the "third mode" reading, after the uniform-autotune fix test.**

The fix test (from https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11793) ran on cw-rno2a with an empty per-fusion autotune folder on all 64 ranks. All 64 ranks compiled one executable (identical compiled-text SHA). Power was even across GPU0 and GPU1-7. Steady updates took **128.7 s and 121.3 s**.

**What it supports**
- **The autotune folder changes the compiled program at autotune level 0.** An earlier run with 151 stale files in process 0's folder had the same cache key and executable fingerprint as the fix test, but a different compiled-text SHA. A matching fingerprint alone does not show two executables are the same.
- **Untuned kernels alone give the slow speed.** About 125 s per update is reached with every rank untuned and identical.

**What it refutes**
- My pre-registered 81-90 s for "all ranks untuned" did not hold.
- **Even power does not mean fast.**
- **"Ranks out of step" is not needed to explain the slow speed.** In the cw-us-east-02a in-job runs, the step time matches the untuned ranks' speed. The low GPU0 power fits rank 0 waiting on them, but that link is not tested.
- **The earlier reading that the cw-rno2a 81-90 s arms run one executable with every rank untuned is wrong.** On the same region's nodes, untuned is about 125 s, not 81-90 s.
  - Caveat: the fix test is the FP32 recipe (key `f80eab37`), and the 81-90 s arms are the BF16 11-18 eager recipe (key `22ca1369`). So this is not a same-dtype comparison. But BF16 in-job runs also sit in the same band: control-prelude 121-122 s and arm A 128.1 s on cw-us-east-02a, and A-r2 121.5-128.4 s on cw-rno2a.

**What may explain the cw-rno2a 81-90 s arms (unverified)**
- The two arms loaded one executable (key `22ca1369`). Process 0 of the first, hung replay40 attempt compiled it against an empty rno2a autotune store.
  - Its node-local `process-0` folder can still hold files left by older jobs. On other cw-rno2a nodes, such folders hold 0 to about 245,000 files, dated Oct 29 to Nov 17.
  - A partly tuned executable from stale files would run between tuned (about 45 s) and untuned (about 125 s).
- A read-only listing of that `process-0` folder, taken at 00:18Z while replay40-r2 ran on the same node, is **inconclusive**.
  - It holds 3,473,443 files. Their mtimes run from 21:14:37Z to 21:21:46Z, during replay40-r2's start-up fetch. 0 files are dated before 20:52Z.
  - The listing cannot show what was in the folder at 20:52Z, for two reasons. First, the uploader (`FineStoreDirectory.flush`) uploads every local file not already in the store, including old ones. Second, the fetch (`fetch_file_set`) rewrites every file in the store's set with a new mtime. So stale files present at the first compile would have been uploaded and then rewritten at 21:14Z.
- **Supporting, not proof:** the same key `22ca1369` exists as three cached copies with different bytes. The cw-rno2a copy is 3,024,491 bytes decompressed. The two cw-us-east-02a copies are 2,984,674 and 2,985,395 bytes. The cw-us-east-02a shared copy ran at 45.5 s. I have not decoded which kernels differ.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖 **In a slow but training in-job-compile run, the first rank on each node is the low-power GPU, on 8 of 8 nodes.**

The run is A-r2 on cw-rno2a: 64 H100, 8 nodes, in-job compile, about 127-135 s per update. I read per-GPU power with `nvidia-smi` on all 8 running pods, read-only. That gave 14 samples per GPU between 00:22:09Z and 00:25:39Z on 2026-11-21, during updates 22-23.

| node (task) | GPU0 median | GPU1-7 medians | GPU0 lowest of 8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 223 W | 458-511 W | 14 of 14 |
| 1 | 237 W | 491-511 W | 14 of 14 |
| 2 | 218 W | 423-458 W | 14 of 14 |
| 3 | 230 W | 466-491 W | 14 of 14 |
| 4 | 223 W | 429-483 W | 14 of 14 |
| 5 | 229 W | 478-510 W | 14 of 14 |
| 6 | 216 W | 441-474 W | 14 of 14 |
| 7 | 215 W | 419-459 W | 14 of 14 |

- **GPU index equals local rank.** All 64 `initialize_jax` lines give `local_device_ids=[process_id mod 8]`. So the low GPU on each node is global process 0, 8, ..., 56. In `_autotune_cache_role`, process 0 is the UPLOADER, which also fetches the tuned set at start, and 8, 16, ..., 56 are FETCHERs. The other 7 ranks per node fetch nothing.
- **Consistent with the per-rank executable split** in the per-rank comparison on https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11793. In that cold compile, ranks with large autotune folders built a cuBLASLt executable, and ranks with sparse folders built a Triton-only one.

**Limits**
- Power is a proxy. I did not count executable variants or read per-rank compiled-text hashes for this run, and it logs no per-rank compile time.
- A variant on one non-first rank would not show up unless its power differed.
- GPU0 also holds more memory (76.0 vs 63.1 GiB) in fast runs too, but fast runs show even power with that same split.
- This run did not stall. It trains at the slow speed, so the power split alone does not mean a hang.

comments.author: karansag
comments.body:
🤖
## Start-up wait on the autotune-fetch ranks grows with the stored autotune set (7 runs, cw-rno2a)

In 7 runs of 64 H100 (8 tasks of 8 GPUs) on `cw-rno2a`, global process 0 and the first process of every other task print their per-fusion autotune cache line, then print nothing until "Detected Iris job context". The other 56 processes print that line within about 1 s. The length of that silent wait follows the size of the stored per-fusion autotune set at start. It does not follow the JAX compilation cache state. This is a correlation over 7 runs in one region, not a controlled test.

**How the numbers were read**
- Wait: printed line time of the first "XLA per-fusion autotune cache" line to the first "Detected Iris job context" line, on local rank 0 of each task, from the hub Finelog task logs. Rank 0 printed 0 lines inside the wait in every task.
- Stored set: `marin_temp_bucket(30, "xla-per-fusion-autotune")/<launch tree_hash>`, the remote root in `iris.jax.compile_cache`. Count and bytes of objects whose last-modified time is before each run's start.
- Roles: in `compile_cache.py`, process 0 is the uploader and `process_index % 8 == 0` are fetchers. Both read the stored set before distributed init. The other 7 processes per task do not.

| Run (FP32 bank optimizer, 150 or 500 updates) | Tree | JAX cache | Stored set at start: objects / bytes | Wait per task, median (min–max) |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Arm E seed 2, compile pre-job | A | miss | 0 / 0 (first object written 1 s after start) | 0.5 s (0–1) |
| Arm E seed 2, main | A | hit | 55 / 110 MB | 207 s (191–230) |
| Arm F seed 2, compile pre-job | B | miss | 0 / 0 (first object written in the start second) | 0 s (0–1) |
| Arm F seed 2, main | B | hit | 45 / 96 MB | 176 s (151–184) |
| Arm E 8-hour, compile pre-job | A | miss | 124 / 281 MB | 478 s (467–519) |
| Arm E 8-hour, second compile pre-job | A | miss | 125 / 281 MB | 496 s (443–518) |
| Arm E 8-hour, main | A | hit | 128 / 281 MB | 523 s (512–882) |

Tree A is `s3://marin-rno2a/tmp/ttl=30d/xla-per-fusion-autotune/5873a3a698/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxla-per-fusion-autotune%2F5873a3a698%2F)). Tree B is `s3://marin-rno2a/tmp/ttl=30d/xla-per-fusion-autotune/44cff8bf4c/` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-rno2a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fxla-per-fusion-autotune%2F44cff8bf4c%2F)). Each tree hash is the git tree of a clean checkout at the training commit.

**What this shows**
- Both runs that started on an empty stored set waited about 0 s, though both were JAX cache misses. The two 8-hour pre-jobs, also misses, waited about 8 min.
- Every run on one commit shares one stored set, so earlier runs on that commit grow it for later ones. Here the arm E seed 2 runs wrote the set that the 8-hour starts later read.
- At about 281 MB the wait was 7.4–8.9 min, with one task at 14.7 min. On a 64-GPU job, the other 56 processes sit idle for that time.

**Not established**
- Whether the fetch itself takes this time. No log line marks the fetch's start or end.
- Whether the wait depends on bytes, object count or node-local file count. The node-local `/cache` contents were not read.
- Whether this matches the 21:14:37–21:21:46Z file-mtime window reported above for a replay40 start.
- A new tree hash starts on an empty set. But, as reported above, at autotune level 0 the autotune folder contents change the compiled program, so changing the tree is not a free fix.

spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

A ~12-hour PRODUCTION-priority sprint (opened 2026-11-21 ~23:00 EST per the user request) to (1) maximize Snowball decode throughput at the 65,536-token request window and (2) size the Snowball RL job as small as possible while keeping training saturated (rollout wait near zero, no time-per-update regression vs the current baseline). Deliverable: a right-sized Snowball RL layout (GPU counts, engine config, all gates) with its measured time per update vs the current allocation and the GPU-hours cost per update. This issue is maintained by the secretary agent from the worker's REPORT.md/STATUS.md; every measured arm is recorded as it lands with reproduction details.

## Description

Context: Snowball RL runs on the Exp4/Exp5 long-loop pools (H100 on cw-rno2a; Snowball also ran on cw-us-east-08a GB200 for the Nov 20 acceptance, job `.305`, 40 GB200). The playbook and lessons come from the Mochi sprint (#11954, closed) and its concurrency-gate table (#11957).

Two phases:
- **Phase 1 — decode throughput at 65k context**: pure serving-benchmark arms with the exact Snowball RL rollout engine config, measured with native vLLM counters (aggregate and per-GPU generated tok/s, per-request tok/s, running/waiting per engine, KV use, prefix-hit rate, preemptions, TTFT) on a long-prompt 65,536-token workload with group-shared prompts as in RL.
- **Phase 2 — right-size the RL job**: shrink rollout GPUs and trainer GPUs step by step on real rollouts with the current Snowball curriculum (Exp4/Exp5 pools); report time per update, rollout wait, engine occupancy, and the per-step split (rollout wait / optimizer / checkpoint / eval). Saturated = trainer rollout wait per step near zero and time per update not regressing vs baseline.

Fixed infrastructure/rules for all arms: PRODUCTION priority; GPU budget ≤ ~2 racks / 128 GPUs in flight without coordinator approval; do not disturb Exp5 SFT (256 H100 on cw-rno2a); one knob per arm, config over code; each arm cancelled with `iris-cancel-own` once measured (25-min windows); Harbor ≤ 512 (Daytona RL org shared, one job ~1/4–1/3 of its 6,000 vCPU); long jobs' IDs go to the coordinator watchdog, no polling loops.

### Reproduction

- Repo: `marin-community/marin`, worktree `/Users/benfeuer/Documents/marin-worktrees/snowball-resize` (branch `benfeuer/snowball-resize` from the long-loop tip); all code/config lands ONLY via `loop-push` onto `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` — no bespoke launchers.
- **Baseline (recorded, milestone 1)**: Snowball RL = **256 GPUs** from the frozen `.51` restart reference — `s3://marin-us-east-08a/marin/users/benfeuer/long-loop-exp3/evidence/restart53/frozen51-reference.json` (sha256 `897f22035802380a63fb748739ae8a66ef208ea67f1fe1e5470bbec417b3e1bb`), consumed by `experiments/post_training/long_loop/exp4.py` `restart_recipe`, mirrored in `experiments/post_training/long_loop/specs/rl.yaml`. Layout: policy+ref 10 nodes × 8 H100 Megatron TP1/PP2/CP5(a2a)/EP8/ETP1; rollout 22 vLLM engines × TP1/PP1/DP8 with EP8 inside each DP8 group = 176 rollout GPUs. Engine config: BF16, FLASH_ATTN, triton MoE, max_num_seqs 64/rank, max_num_batched_tokens 8192, gpu_memory_utilization 0.75, prefix caching on, chunked prefill on, CUDA graphs on, max_model_len 102400, hermes tool parser, enable_thinking, routed-expert capture. Gates: full_batch, staleness 2, max_in_flight 32, quotas 32/32 (Exp4 plan 22/42), Harbor `n_concurrent_trials` 256, checkpoint/eval every 2 steps. **No baseline measurement exists** (the `.51` RL attempt failed 2026-11-17; Exp4/Exp5 RL never launched; Exp5 SFT job `/benfeuer/mochi-exp5-2026.11.21.113` runs untouched). Frozen-reference receipt: `frozen51-reference-20261122.json`.
- Per-arm details (branch/commit, config paths, launch commands, Iris job IDs, S3 receipts with Filer links, finelog queries) are added below as arms land, in the same format as #11954. First two arms declared: **S1 control** — the exact RL engine shape as a pure serving benchmark (8 H100, one engine: TP1/DP8/EP8, seqs 64, batched 8192, HBM 0.75; synthetic 65,536-token-window prompts, prompt group size 8, output 1024, concurrency 512, warmup 120 s, measure 1500 s); **S2** — S1 with `gpu_memory_utilization` 0.75→0.90. Submission via the standard Iris CLI at PRODUCTION on cw-rno2a; each arm cancelled after its measured window.
- Worker: OpenCode session `ses_dfe9b2626ffeHwqZI0Gd8yCX2L` (cc's the secretary on every arm, result, and decision); Exp2 (Codex 01a16e8e) keeps babysitting the long loop (Exp5) — untouched.
- Authoritative running records: `/Users/benfeuer/Documents/experiments/active/snowball-resize/{BRIEF.md,REPORT.md,STATUS.md}` (REPORT.md top table authoritative once arms land).

## Hypothesis or Goal

Maximize Snowball decode throughput at 65k context, then right-size the Snowball RL job: the smallest GPU allocation that keeps training saturated (rollout wait ≈ 0 per step, no time-per-update regression vs the current baseline). Deliverable: the right-sized layout with measured time per update vs the current allocation and GPU-hours per update.

## Status

- **S3 FINAL (+16.5% per-GPU over S2) — and PHASE 2 begins** (S3 job `/benfeuer/snowball-resize-decode-seqs128-20261122a`, source `e00de8519b`; seqs 64→128 at HBM 0.90): aggregate 15,091.2 gen tok/s; **1,886.4 per GPU**; request decode 15.33 tok/s (TPOT 65.3 ms); TTFT 2.08 s mean / 1.75 p50 / 7.36 p99; running 124.1/128 mean (cap-bound, p95 128); waiting 0.17; KV 83.5% mean / 89.6% max; prefix 99.97%; 22,465 succeeded / 0 failed. Fix landed via `loop-push` at `43f9042f3c30a49a9e34a5ef2cecc62a880d58aa` ("Honor declared route quotas in adopted RL rounds"): `build_run` now preserves the round's declared `consumed_route_quotas` (smoke derives quotas from its shrunken batch; full runs fail fast unless the declaration partitions the batch, mirroring vendor/skyrl `RolloutBufferConfig.__post_init__` "positive and sum to batch_size"). - S3 submitted 23:38:15 UTC (`…-decode-seqs128-20261122a`; log `s3-seqs128-submission.log`); FINAL results in the table below.

Workload: synthetic ~64.5k-token prompts (65,536 window), output 1024, prompt group size 8, closed-loop concurrency 512, warmup 120 s, measure 1500 s, request timeout 1200 s. tpu-inference wheel pair, then serves Qwen3-0.6B at tensor parallel size 8 on
`v6e-8`. This makes each refresh depend on an eight-chip slice. Qwen3-0.6B is
already the smallest model used by this test; the smaller resource shape is
tensor parallel size 4 on `v6e-4`.

[A previous fork refresh passed the served-Qwen3 test on `v6e-4`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8616),
and [an earlier cold wheel consumer passed 22 of 22 requests on
`v6e-4`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8323#issuecomment-5348879398).
The current public wheel pair has only been tested on `v6e-8`, so prove that
exact pair on `v6e-4` before changing the refresh procedure.

Keep the tpu-inference nightly at tensor parallel size 8 on its eight-chip TPU
alternatives. The nightly continues to cover the TP8 path while the refresh
test checks that Marin can install and use the exact release on a smaller
slice.

Done when:

- The exact wheel pair selected by a refresh is installed in a fresh `uvx`
  environment and served on `v6e-4` at tensor parallel size 4.
- The server becomes healthy, a real model request succeeds, and the receipt
  records the release, both wheel versions, Iris job and task IDs, and evidence
  that the job stopped and released the TPU.
- After that run passes, the refresh procedure uses `v6e-4` and tensor parallel
  size 4. It still runs only one TPU test and consumes the published wheels
  without rebuilding them.
- The fork policy diagram and test table name the new refresh hardware.
- The tpu-inference nightly keeps its TP8 coverage.

spillover_issues.author: yonromai
spillover_issues.body:
A weekly GPU vLLM refresh currently reserves accelerators in two places. The
vLLM release flow validates the exact x86_64 and aarch64 candidate wheels
through Iris on H100 and GB200. Marin then validates the same candidate with a
Snowball output comparison and a bounded Qwen3 serving test on H100. Both H100
gates install the candidate wheel and exercise a live serving path.

Move accelerator qualification for a GPU wheel candidate into the Marin
refresh. The vLLM workflow should build immutable x86_64 and aarch64 candidate
wheels without reserving an accelerator. Marin should qualify those exact
wheel bytes on H100 and GB200, run the Snowball and Qwen3 integration checks,
and record one result that binds the source commit, wheel URLs and digests, and
both hardware results. H100 and GB200 remain required because they test
different architecture-specific wheels.

[#7995](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7995) records the
current two-architecture release gate and immutable-wheel promotion. It does
not explain why the later Marin H100 test is a separate gate.

Done when:

- Building a GPU wheel candidate does not reserve an accelerator.
- Marin tests the exact x86_64 wheel on H100 and the exact aarch64 wheel on
  GB200. The qualification preserves the current install, native-extension,
  runtime, and serving checks needed to catch wheel or architecture failures.
- One result identifies the source commit, wheel URLs and digests, H100 and
  GB200 results, and the Marin Snowball and Qwen3 results.
- A failed or missing hardware result blocks promotion.
- Promotion reuses the qualified wheel bytes without rebuilding them.
- Ordinary fork PR CI, scheduled nightlies, and the TPU release flow are
  unchanged.

cc @rjpower

spillover_issues.author: RohithKuditipudi
spillover_issues.body:
A caller that runs `execute()` on a worker thread has no way, from any other thread, to make it stop early — whether the pipeline's results are no longer needed or the process is shutting down. If the worker job that `execute()` launches never schedules (no accelerator capacity), the call blocks for 12 hours and nothing can release it sooner.

What `execute()` launches: on a fresh context it calls `_start_pool()`, which submits a coordinator job (`execution.py:502`), tells it to spawn a worker job, and waits for the first worker to register — up to `ZEPHYR_WORKERS_READY_WAIT`, default 12 h (`execution.py:532-533`). The handles to these jobs are held in variables local to the call (`execution.py:646`); nothing is assigned to the context object, and `self._state` stays `NEW`.

What `shutdown()` does: it stops what the context has registered — the pool that only `start()` assigns (`execution.py:550`) — and returns immediately for state `NEW` (`execution.py:689`). During `execute()` it therefore has no effect: the jobs it would need to stop are reachable only from inside the blocked call. Calling `start()` first does not help: `start()` holds `_state_lock` across the same first-worker wait (`execution.py:550`), and `shutdown()` blocks acquiring that lock (`execution.py:684`).

What changed: before #7145, `execute()` stored its coordinator job on the instance (`self._coordinator_job`) and `shutdown()` terminated that job — workers included, via cascading termination — from any thread at any point in the call. #7145 moved the pool into the `execute()` call and rewrote `shutdown()` around the `NEW`/`OWNER` state machine; cancelling a running `execute()` was dropped with no replacement.

Observed in production, 2026-08-22/23: a driver needed to cancel `execute()` calls whose work other pools had already completed. The v5litepod worker jobs never scheduled (`Insufficient TPUs (need 4, available 0)`); `shutdown()` at ~02:00 UTC had no effect, and each blocked call held its thread until the 12 h wait expired at ~11:20 UTC. The only unstick was killing the coordinator jobs out-of-band.

Done when: `shutdown()` (or an equivalent) promptly cancels a running `execute()`, including one still waiting for its first worker. One shape: register the coordinator group on the context at creation, before the blocking waits; deregister when the pool ends; have `shutdown()` stop registered live groups regardless of state.

spillover_issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
spillover_issues.body:
508 of the 1,000 `time_intervals` rows of the generated Reasoning Gym source grade only on the day they were generated. On a later day [the grade script](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/reasoning_gym_grade.py#L55-L57) exits 1 with `ValueError: Regenerated entry differs from the recorded entry` for every reply, the row's own answer included, and [grading](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/runtime/grading.py#L350-L353) records an infrastructure error. [Training](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L191-L209) then leaves the rollout out of the loss. `snowball-100k` draws 20,800 rows of this source; I did not count its `time_intervals` rows.

Reproduce:

1. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   PYTHONHASHSEED=0 uv run --package marin-verifyit --extra reasoning-gym python - <<'EOF'
   import sys

   sys.path.insert(0, "experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym")
   import generate
   import reasoning_gym

   task = "time_intervals"
   data = reasoning_gym.create_dataset(task, size=generate.ROWS_PER_TASK, seed=generate.task_seed(task))
   entry = generate.encoded(data[2])
   print(entry["question"])
   print(entry["metadata"]["start_time"], "|", entry["metadata"]["end_time"])
   time_only = ("time", "time_seconds", "time_ms")
   print(sum(data[index]["metadata"]["task_type"] in time_only for index in range(generate.ROWS_PER_TASK)))
   EOF
   ```

2. The first line is a question with times only: `A meeting started at 01:01:14 and ended at 06:10:42. How long was the meeting? Answer in HH:MM:SS.` The second line is the entry's `metadata.start_time` and `metadata.end_time`. They carry the date of the run, for example `2026-11-16 01:01:14 | 2026-11-16 06:10:42`. The third line is `508`, the number of entries of the task types `time`, `time_seconds` and `time_ms`.
3. The row's contract stores the entry as encoded on the generation day, so on a later day the comparison at L56 fails for these entries.

Expected: a row's own answer scores 1.0 on any day.

`reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 parses the time-only strings with `dateutil.parser.parse` (`reasoning_gym/arithmetic/time_intervals.py` L104-L105), and `dateutil` fills a missing date with the current day in the process's local time. The question and the answer are the same on every day. [The converter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/tasks.py#L261-L262) rejects an entry whose `reproducible` flag is false, but [the generator](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/generate.py#L141-L150) sets that flag by regenerating the entry in the same process, so it is true for these rows.

I did not grade a stored row. I encoded the 1,000 entries with `datetime.now()` fixed to 2026-11-04 inside `dateutil`'s parser and ran the grade script on 2026-11-16: 508 regenerated entries differ from the recorded ones, entry 2 exits 1 on its own answer, and entry 0 (task type `datetime`) prints 1.0. Among the first 200 entries of each of the 104 generated tasks, regenerated on another day and in two other time zones, no other task has entries that pass the `reproducible` flag and differ.

spillover_issues.body:
Four generated Reasoning Gym tasks give full reward to a reply that does not depend on the question. `reasoning_gym_generated` holds 1,000 rows of each.

- `game_of_life_halting`: every non-blank reply scores 1.0 on all 1,000 entries. The scorer compares `bool(reply)` with `bool(answer)`, and every answer is the string `True` or `False`. [The generator](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/generate.py#L77-L86) records the reward of the fixed wrong answer `definitely wrong` for every row. For these 1,000 rows the recorded reward is 1.0, and [`convert_generated`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d83e7766c5a5b9bec43cdd26eccc71a54dcf9bfd/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym/tasks.py#L256-L271) stores the record without reading it.
- `complex_arithmetic`: the reply `NaN` scores 1.0 on all 1,000 entries. The scorer returns `min(1.0, math.exp(-distance))`, which is 1.0 when the distance is NaN.
- `coin_flip`: the reply `0` scores 1.0 on 939 of the 1,000 entries. The scorer of `reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 gives partial reward for a matching prefix and divides by the length of the shorter string, so the one-character reply `0` matches every answer that starts with `0.`.
- `propositional_logic`: the reply `P ∨ Q` scores 1.0 on 820 of the 1,000 entries. The scorer accepts any conclusion that follows from the premises, and a disjunction that names a premise follows from it.

Reproduce:

1. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   PYTHONHASHSEED=0 uv run --package marin-verifyit --extra reasoning-gym python - <<'EOF'
   import sys

   sys.path.insert(0, "experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/reasoning_gym")
   import generate
   import reasoning_gym

   replies = (
       ("game_of_life_halting", "x"),
       ("complex_arithmetic", "NaN"),
       ("coin_flip", "0"),
       ("propositional_logic", "P ∨ Q"),
   )
   for task, reply in replies:
       data = reasoning_gym.create_dataset(task, size=generate.ROWS_PER_TASK, seed=generate.task_seed(task))
       score = reasoning_gym.get_score_answer_fn(task)
       print(task, repr(reply), sum(score(reply, data[index]) == 1.0 for index in range(generate.ROWS_PER_TASK)))
   EOF
   ```

2. It prints `game_of_life_halting 'x' 1000`, `complex_arithmetic 'NaN' 1000`, `coin_flip '0' 939` and `propositional_logic 'P ∨ Q' 820`.

Expected: a constant reply does not earn full reward.

The recorded wrong answer scores 0 on `complex_arithmetic` and `coin_flip` and 0.05 or 0.25 on `propositional_logic`, so that record shows only the first of the four. Two of the four are in the Nemotron blend's part of the released validation panel (`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data`): with the panel's own grade script, `P ∨ Q` scores 1.0 on six of its seven `propositional_logic` tasks and `NaN` on its one `complex_arithmetic` task.

I tried 44 constant replies on the first 100 entries of every generated task. No fifth task gives the full reward on more than a quarter of the entries to a constant that is not the entry's answer.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 A fifth task belongs on this list: `puzzle24`. The reply `1*2*3*4` scores 1.0 on all 1,000 of its generated entries. The scorer of `reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 (`reasoning_gym/games/puzzle24.py` L114-L132) checks that the reply evaluates to 24 and contains four numbers between 1 and 10. It does not read the entry's numbers. Five of the 1,000 entries have the numbers 1, 2, 3 and 4. The recorded wrong answer `definitely wrong` scores 0.01 on every entry, so that record does not show it.

The last paragraph of the issue says that no fifth task pays a constant on more than a quarter of its entries. None of the 44 constants I tried evaluates to 24, so that sweep could not find this task.

To check, add `("puzzle24", "1*2*3*4")` to `replies` in the script above. It prints `puzzle24 '1*2*3*4' 1000`. `puzzle24` is not in the released validation panel.

spillover_issues.author: XiaoyuanWang111
spillover_issues.body:
14,062 of the 65,559 tasks of `NeMo:predicted-action` (21.4%) expect a string argument of 10 or more words that occurs nowhere in the request. The source scores a reply 1 only for the exact function name with exact JSON arguments ([`nemo_tool_calls.py` L37](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemo_tool_calls.py#L37), [`grade_predicted_action_candidate`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_predicted_action.py#L47-L61)), so a reply passes such a task only when it writes that string character for character. In 13,738 of the 14,062 tasks the only such arguments are `summary` or `issue_summary`, with a median of 32 words. They belong to calls that hand the conversation to a person, such as `transfer_to_human_agent`.

EvalLite's `agents` family is 165 tasks of this source ([recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/47383aec90fd93895cf76ea9cad65b84717d8aae/experiments/post_training/task_curation/recipes/eval-lite.json#L78-L86)). At the source's rate about 35 of them are such tasks, and every checkpoint scores 0 on them. The recipe's seeded order selects 44 when I apply it to the source without the overlap exclusions; I cannot read the training and development sets that the exclusions use.

Reproduce:

1. One task, row 94,789 of the pinned `train.jsonl`. From the repository root, run:

   ```bash
   uv run --package marin-verifyit python - <<'EOF'
   from verifyit.modes.grade_predicted_action import grade_predicted_action_candidate
   from verifyit.spec import FunctionCall, PredictedActionSpec

   expected = (
       "User inherited portfolio with appreciated securities, questions about step-up basis calculation "
       "and tax implications of significant gains."
   )
   spec = PredictedActionSpec(
       expected_calls=(FunctionCall("transfer_to_human_advisor", {"summary": expected, "urgency": "medium"}),)
   )
   replies = (
       expected,
       expected.rstrip("."),
       "The user inherited a portfolio of appreciated securities and asks how the step-up in basis is "
       "calculated and what tax the gains carry.",
   )
   for reply in replies:
       call = FunctionCall("transfer_to_human_advisor", {"summary": reply, "urgency": "medium"})
       print(grade_predicted_action_candidate(spec, (call,)).reward, reply)
   EOF
   ```

   It prints `1.0` for the expected call, `0.0` for the same call without the final period of the summary, and `0.0` for a paraphrase of the summary.

2. The count. The command downloads the pinned `train.jsonl` (1.75 GB) and takes about two minutes:

   ```bash
   uv run --package marin-taskcompendium python - <<'EOF'
   import json
   import statistics

   from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
   from taskcompendium.identity import canonical_sha256
   from taskcompendium.importers.nemo_predicted_action import DATASET, REVISION, import_row


   def texts(value):
       """Every string in a JSON value, and every string inside a string that is itself JSON."""
       if isinstance(value, str):
           yield value
           try:
               value = json.loads(value)
           except ValueError:
               return
           if not isinstance(value, dict | list):
               return
       for item in value.values() if isinstance(value, dict) else value if isinstance(value, list) else ():
           yield from texts(item)


   tasks, free_rows, long_rows, summary_only, longest = 0, 0, 0, 0, []
   with open(hf_hub_download(DATASET, "train.jsonl", revision=REVISION, repo_type="dataset")) as rows:
       for line in rows:
           row = json.loads(line)
           try:
               task = import_row(row, canonical_sha256(row))
           except ValueError:
               continue
           tasks += 1
           seen = "\n".join(texts(row["responses_create_params"]))
           free = {
               key: len(value.split())
               for call in task.grader.parameters["expected_calls"]
               for key, value in call["arguments"].items()
               if isinstance(value, str) and len(value.split()) >= 2 and value not in seen
           }
           free_rows += bool(free)
           if free and max(free.values()) >= 10:
               long_rows += 1
               summary_only += {key for key, words in free.items() if words >= 10} <= {"summary", "issue_summary"}
               longest.append(max(free.values()))
   print(tasks, free_rows, long_rows, summary_only, statistics.median(longest))
   EOF
   ```

   It prints `65559 15164 14062 13738 32.0`: the tasks, the tasks that expect a string of two or more words that is absent from the request, the tasks where such a string has 10 or more words, the tasks among those where only `summary` or `issue_summary` holds such a string, and the median word count of the longest such string.

Expected: a task whose expected call holds free text is left out of the source, or its free-text arguments are compared by a rule that a correct reply can meet.

NeMo Gym's verifier for this dataset compares strings of two or more words by word overlap, with a threshold of 0.1 ([config L7-L8](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym/blob/69a514999667cebee03d8fd8bd0aec996a54a504/resources_servers/single_step_tool_use_with_argument_comparison/configs/single_step_tool_use_with_argument_comparison.yaml#L7-L8), [`_compare_strings`](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym/blob/69a514999667cebee03d8fd8bd0aec996a54a504/resources_servers/single_step_tool_use_with_argument_comparison/common/verification_utils.py#L597-L634)). The paraphrase of step 1 has an overlap of 0.225 under that rule. The dataset stores 16 rewards per row for Qwen3-235B (`qwen_235b_info`). Their mean is 0.40 on the 14,062 rows and 0.33 on the 46,162 rows whose expected string arguments are all single tokens.
